section_summary: This section comprises registers of outgoing telegrams and despatches from the American Embassy in Tokyo for November 1940 (along with duplicate archival copies of those lists), Despatch No. 5218 transmitting Embassy Report No. 1670 on political, foreign, and economic conditions in Japan during November 1940, and telegrams and cross-reference sheets from late 1940 and early 1941. The core monthly report documents mounting Japanese-American tension over bombings of American mission property in China, military interference with American firms and consular officials (notably the detention of Vice Consul Rinden and Melville Jacoby at Hanoi), Japanese recognition of Wang Ching-wei's regime at Nanking, the mission to the Netherlands East Indies, and domestic events such as the 2600th imperial anniversary, the death of Prince Saionji, and the Ten-Year Economic Plan. Concluding documents address Japanese cabinet instability, rumors surrounding Foreign Minister Matsuoka's tenure, and senior personnel changes in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

subfiles.about: Sequential register of telegrams Nos. 1084 through 1251 sent by the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State during November 1940.
subfiles.summary: Provides a chronological log of telegrams transmitted to Washington during November 1940, specifying telegram number, dispatch date and time, and subject matter. Major subjects include the 2600th imperial anniversary festivities, Japanese air raids on American property and commercial aircraft in China, the evacuation of American dependents and missionaries from Japan and Korea, the designation and appointment of Admiral Kichisaburo Nomura as Ambassador to Washington, exchange control issues, the arrest of Vice Consul Rinden and Melville Jacoby in Hanoi, and diplomatic moves involving the Axis powers. The log concludes on November 30 with telegram No. 1251 noting the appointment of Kenkichi Yoshizawa to lead the trade mission to the Netherlands East Indies.
subfiles.title: Telegrams Sent to the Department, November, 1940

subfiles.about: Sequential register of despatches Nos. 5106 through 5181 sent by the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State during November 1940.
subfiles.summary: Catalogs formal despatches forwarded from Tokyo to Washington in November 1940, indicating despatch numbers, dates, and subjects. The documents treat key political, military, and commercial matters including the New Structure, trade restrictions in North China, the Kobayashi Mission to Batavia, damage to American mission properties in Chungking, Hosueh, Shasi, Miaochien, and Chenki, the detention of Greek shipping, and regular weekly commercial and financial summaries. Administrative despatches concerning embassy personnel leaves of absence, visa reporting, and chancery maintenance are also recorded.
subfiles.title: List of Despatches Sent to the Department, November, 1940

subfiles.about: Comprehensive monthly report surveying Japanese foreign relations, military campaigns, and internal political and economic developments during November 1940.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits Report No. 1670 detailing Embassy representations over Japanese attacks on CNAC passenger aircraft, alteration of Chinese courts in Shanghai's French Concession, interference with the Universal Leaf Tobacco Company, missionary agitation, exchange restrictions, the arrest of Vice Consul Rinden and Melville Jacoby at Hanoi, and demands upon Indochina. Reviews the appointment of Admiral Nomura as Ambassador to Washington, the reaction to President Roosevelt's reelection, the conclusion of the basic treaty recognizing the Wang Ching-wei regime in Nanking, military troop movements in South China, oil negotiations in Batavia, and Thai-Indochina border controversies. Summarizes domestic political developments, including the nationwide 2600th imperial anniversary celebrations, the passing of Prince Kimmochi Saionji, the Diet's 50th anniversary, the proclamation of the Ten-Year Economic Plan for Greater East Asia, the creation of the Foreign Office South Seas Bureau, and institutional conflicts surrounding the New Structure.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5218 transmitting Report No. 1670: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of November 1940

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of the chronological register of telegrams Nos. 1084 through 1251 sent by the Tokyo Embassy to the State Department during November 1940.
subfiles.summary: Represents a second archival copy of the chronological index of outgoing telegrams from Tokyo for November 1940, covering telegrams Nos. 1084 through 1251 (omitting page 7, which contained Nos. 1204 to 1222 in the primary sequence). Registers telegram dispatch numbers, dates, times, and subject summaries regarding diplomatic representations, missionary detentions and evacuations, press analyses, and ambassadorial conferences. Provides a secondary filing duplicate of the telegram list found earlier in the volume.
subfiles.title: Telegrams Sent to the Department, November, 1940 (Duplicate Copy)

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of the register of despatches Nos. 5106 through 5181 sent by the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State during November 1940.
subfiles.summary: Reproduces the complete chronological schedule of despatches Nos. 5106 through 5181 transmitted by the Tokyo Embassy to Washington in November 1940. Lists document numbers, submission dates, and titles covering political developments, missionary bomb damage claims, the Kobayashi economic mission, commercial and financial reviews, and embassy staff administration. Constitutes an archival duplicate of pages 597 through 601.
subfiles.title: List of Despatches Sent to the Department, November, 1940 (Duplicate Copy)

subfiles.about: Reports the resignation of Nobusuke Kishi as Vice Minister of Commerce and Industry and the appointment of Shinichi Kojima as his successor.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo (via Shanghai)
subfiles.summary: Transmits plain telegram No. 7 reporting that Vice Minister of Commerce and Industry Nobusuke Kishi submitted his resignation on December 28, 1940, to the Overseas Minister during the absence from Tokyo of Commerce Minister Ichizo Kobayashi. Notes press announcements that Shinichi Kojima, Chief of the Trade Bureau in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, would be officially named as Kishi's successor in the Official Gazette on January 4, 1941.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 7 regarding Resignation of Nobusuke Kishi

subfiles.about: Reports confidential diplomatic information from the French Ambassador indicating that Foreign Minister Matsuoka is expected to resign soon.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Relays strictly confidential intelligence received from French Ambassador Arsène-Henry, who was informed by a prominent Japanese Foreign Office adviser that Foreign Minister Yosuke Matsuoka would resign within the week due to inability to implement his policies. Reports that Toshio Shiratori was ruled out as successor because he was preparing to seek the premiership, and that General Yoshitsugu Tatekawa, Ambassador to Moscow, was viewed as the most probable replacement. Ambassador Grew comments that although lacking external confirmation, he has maintained and still believes that Matsuoka will not remain long in office.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 76 regarding Political Forecasts on Foreign Minister Matsuoka

subfiles.about: Departmental digest of Tokyo telegram No. 76 regarding the anticipated resignation of Foreign Minister Yosuke Matsuoka.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Summarizes Ambassador Grew's strictly confidential telegram No. 76 concerning reports that Foreign Minister Yosuke Matsuoka is expected to resign because of policy frustration. Highlights informant statements that Toshio Shiratori was not seeking the post in order to protect his prospects for Prime Minister, leaving General Tatekawa as the probable successor. Records the Department's notation of the Embassy's ongoing forecast of Matsuoka's impending political downfall.
subfiles.title: Digest of Tokyo Telegram No. 76

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a Naval Attaché report on the fall of the Yonai Cabinet and formation of the Second Konoye Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Provides a cross-reference entry indexing Naval Attaché Report No. 22 dated August 7, 1940, filed under decimal file 894.002/439. References the resignation of the Yonai Cabinet and the organization of the Second Konoye Cabinet, noting the composition of the incoming ministry and its projected policy shifts.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Naval Attaché Report No. 22 on the Second Konoye Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a telegram regarding Japanese business opposition to the Tripartite Pact.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Cross-references Tokyo telegram No. 1929 sent at 7 p.m. on October 2, 1940, originally filed under decimal file 762.9411/77. Notes substantial undercurrent opposition to the German-Italian-Japanese alliance from Japanese commercial interests owing to the severe disruption of economic relations with Great Britain and the United States.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Tokyo Telegram No. 1929 on Business Opposition to Tripartite Pact

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a telegram reporting rumors of Japanese cabinet collapse and General Itagaki's appointment as War Minister.
subfiles.from: J. Hall Paxton, American Consulate, Nanking
subfiles.summary: Indexes Nanking telegram No. 133 sent at 11 a.m. on December 13, 1940, filed under decimal file 793.94/16370. Transmits rumors from Nanking indicating that the Japanese cabinet was about to collapse and that General Seishiro Itagaki was expected to become the next Minister of War.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Nanking Telegram No. 133 on Cabinet Collapse Rumors
